repository.name: jobFynder-BE-nestJS
repository.description: This is for BE rewamp to nestJS from nodeJS

commits.message:
feat(resume-intelligence): build the real CORE <-> Hermes chain for Resume Builder + Matching

Before this, the Resume Builder frontend (81 components under
src/components/components/private/resume-builder/) had zero backend
wiring for any of its AI/intelligence features -- confirmed via a full
audit (no fetch/axios/useQuery calls anywhere in that tree; every
screen renders from ~1,766 lines of static "constants" mock data).
Meanwhile HERMES-800 (Resume Builder) and HERMES-300 (Matching) already
existed on Hermes, tagged, RBAC-protected, and live-verified -- nothing
on CORE had ever called them. This is that missing chain: the actual
HERMES-810 "end-to-end" work, not a test of something that already
existed.

New module: src/resume-intelligence/
- hermes-client.service.ts: a thin authenticated relay to Hermes.
  Bearer token (scoped: understanding:parse/read, submissions:evaluate,
  resume_builder:read/analyze/suggest, matching:evaluate -- the last
  four added to the existing jobfynder-core RBAC user on Hermes in this
  same pass, since the original HERMES-100 RBAC-fix token only had the
  first two). Does not reshape Hermes's response -- callers get the
  exact shape documented in Hermes's own OpenAPI schema.
- resume-intelligence.controller.ts: 7 endpoints behind JwtAuthGuard --
  parse, summary/suggest, bullets/suggest, tailor, quality/analyze,
  skills/suggest (all HERMES-800), and match (HERMES-300, powers
  "Align to Role" and "Job match & gap analysis" in the frontend mock).

configuration.ts/env.validation.ts: added HERMES_API_TOKEN/
HERMES_API_BASE_URL, same pattern as the LITELLM_* additions earlier.

Request/response shapes were pulled directly from Hermes's live
GET /openapi.json before writing any DTO -- not guessed. (Worth noting:
an earlier doc I wrote today had a "text" vs "content" field-name bug
for a different Hermes endpoint; pulling the real schema this time was
deliberate, not optional.)

Two real bugs found and fixed during live verification, not before:
1. The jobfynder-core RBAC token (provisioned during the HERMES-100 fix)
   didn't have resume_builder:*/matching:evaluate permissions -- every
   call 403'd until this was added directly via
   /opt/hermes-runtime/access-control/users.json on INTEL-1 (no
   restart needed, permissions are read from disk per-request).
2. CORE's CsrfGuard checks request origin before considering its own
   bearer-token exemption -- a request with no Origin/Referer header
   gets rejected before the guard even reaches the "Bearer tokens skip
   CSRF" check. Not touched (pre-existing, unrelated code, and the
   real frontend always sends an Origin header) -- worked around in
   testing by sending Origin: https://testing.jobfynder.com, and noted
   here so nobody rediscovers this by surprise.

Verified: scripts/verifyResumeIntelligence.mjs exercises all 7
endpoints plus a negative-auth path against the live deployed server
with a real (short-lived, test-only) JWT for an existing user. All
passing, including a real HERMES-300 match call that correctly flagged
Kubernetes as a missing required skill -- the exact "Missing/Weak
Skills" shape the frontend mock already expects.

Not done in this pass: wiring the frontend's 81 mock-data components to
these new endpoints (started separately, see the FE branch), and the
credits/ATS-51-system-simulation/achievement-library/collaboration/
performance-analytics/variants features shown in the frontend mocks --
none of those have a Hermes capability to wire to; they're real,
separate product features with no backend anywhere, out of scope for
"HERMES-810 and 300."
